style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The first psalm of the Egyptian Hallel (113-118), sung at the Passover table for well over two thousand years -- so it was almost certainly on Jesus' lips the night He was betrayed. Its structure is a single stunning contrast. First the height: the LORD's name praised from now to forever and from sunrise to sunset, the LORD high above all nations, His glory above the heavens, enthroned so high He must stoop even to look at the sky. Then the descent: this same God reaches down into the dust and the ash heap -- the refuse heap outside the town where, by long Eastern custom, the destitute bedded down in the warm ash -- and lifts the beggar up to seat him among princes; He takes the barren woman, the ancient world's picture of shame, and sets her at her own table as a joyful mother. Hannah sang it first at Shiloh; Mary sang it again in the hill country of Judah, in Elizabeth's house. The incomparability of God -- 'who is like the LORD our God?' -- is defined not by how high He sits but by how low He is willing to reach.

1.text: Praise the LORD! Praise Him, you servants of the LORD; praise the name of the LORD.
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD ['Hallelujah', halelu-Yah, the KJV margin]. Praise [halal], O ye servants [ebed] of the LORD [YHWH], praise the name [shem] of the LORD.
1.notes: The Egyptian Hallel (113-118) opens with its signature word, halelu-Yah (H1984, H3050). Psalms 113-114 were sung before the Passover meal and 115-118 after it, so the Hallel framed the Upper Room's cup on both sides (cf. Matthew 26:30). Three halal's in one verse, addressed to the avde YHWH (H5650): praise is the servants' job description.

2.text: Blessed be the name of the LORD, from now on and for all time.
2.amp: Blessed [barak] be the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH] from this time forth [attah -- now] and for [ad] evermore [olam].
2.notes: me-attah ve-ad-olam (H6258, H5704, H5769): from this now until forever -- praise given a start-date (today) and no end-date. The shem (H8034) is the revealed character; to barak (H1288) it is to speak well of who He has shown Himself to be.

3.text: From the place the sun rises to the place it sets, the name of the LORD is to be praised.
3.amp: From the rising [mizrach] of the sun [shemesh] unto the going down [mabo] of the same the LORD'S [YHWH] name [shem] is to be praised [halal].
3.notes: Verse 2 gave praise its time-span; verse 3 gives its geography: mi-mizrach shemesh ad mevoo (H4217, H8121, H3996), east to west, every longitude. Malachi 1:11 makes the same span a prophecy of Gentile worship.

4.text: The LORD is high above all the nations; His glory is above the heavens.
4.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is high [rum] above all nations [goy], and His glory [kabod] above the heavens [shamayim].
4.notes: rum (H7311), exalted -- above kol goyim (H1471) politically, above shamayim (H8064) cosmically, His kabod (H3519) higher than the sky. The height is stated first so that the stooping of verse 6 lands with its full weight.

5.text: Who is like the LORD our God, who is enthroned so high,
5.amp: Who is like unto the LORD [YHWH] our God [Elohim], who dwells ['exalteth himself to dwell', gabah yashab, the KJV margin] on high,
5.notes: mi ka-YHWH -- the Red Sea's question (cf. Exodus 15:11), asked again. ha-magbihi la-shabet (H1361, H3427): He makes His seat high -- and the incomparability is about to be defined not by His height but by what He does from it.

6.text: yet stoops down low to look upon the heavens and the earth?
6.amp: Who humbles [shaphel -- stoops, makes low] Himself to behold [raah] the things that are in heaven [shamayim], and in the earth [eretz]!
6.notes: The psalm's astonishment: ha-mashpili lirot (H8213, H7200) -- He must lower Himself even to LOOK at the heavens. If the sky is beneath His notice, His attention to a dust-heap beggar (v. 7) is condescension past measure (cf. Philippians 2:6-8).

7.text: He raises the poor up out of the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap,
7.amp: He raises up [qum] the poor [dal -- the weak, the thin] out of the dust [afar], and lifts [rum] the needy [evyon] out of the dunghill [ashpot -- the ash heap, the refuse pile];
7.notes: Hannah's song nearly word for word (cf. 1 Samuel 2:8): the dal and the evyon (H1800, H34) -- the frail and the destitute -- qum'd from afar (H6965, H6083) and rum'd from the ashpot (H7311, H830), the refuse heap where, by long Eastern custom, the destitute bedded down in the warm ash. The same rum that described God's height (v. 4) is now applied to the beggar.

8.text: to seat him among princes -- among the princes of His own people.
8.amp: That he may set [yashab -- seat] him with princes [nadib -- nobles], even with the princes of His people [am].
8.notes: yashab (H3427) again -- the God who 'seats Himself on high' (v. 5) seats the beggar im nedibim (H5081), at the nobles' table. Not charity but promotion; Joseph from the pit to the throne room is the pattern, and the Magnificat's 'exalted them of low degree' is the echo (cf. Luke 1:52).

9.text: He settles the barren woman in a home of her own, as the joyful mother of children. Praise the LORD!
9.amp: He makes the barren woman [aqereth -- the childless wife] to keep house ['to dwell in an house', yashab bayith, the KJV margin], and to be a joyful [sameach] mother [em] of children [ben]. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
9.notes: The third yashab: the aqeret (H6135) settled in her bayith (H1004) -- Sarah, Rachel, Hannah, Elizabeth, each barren woman given a seat at her own table as em ha-banim semechah (H517, H1121, H8056), the glad mother. The Hallel's first psalm ends where it began, halelu-Yah, having shown what the high God stoops to do.
